about: simple terminal UI for git commands
hook: Git, but you'll actually enjoy it
pitch: A terminal UI that lets you stage single lines with a space bar press and run interactive rebases in a few keystrokes. It shows branches, commits, and changes at a glance so you stop memorizing git commands.

about: An agent skill that finds open-source issues where your PR can actually land — interest-driven scouting, acceptance evidence, tested patches, with human gates on what to pursue and what to publish
hook: Land your PRs automatically
pitch: landable scouts GitHub Trending repos in your star range, ranks issues where outsiders get merged, and verifies the fix lives in the target repo. You only pick an issue and approve the final patch, letting the agent handle the rest. 🚀

about: a shell-pipe language for image manipulation, built on libvips
hook: Fast image pipelines from your shell.
pitch: Build batch image pipelines right in your terminal. One pipe can read files or URLs, resize, sharpen and write as WebP, all in a single libvips pass that stays low on memory. Try the TypeScript-based CLI today.

about: [CVPR 2026] PersonaLive! : Expressive Portrait Image Animation for Live Streaming
builder: GVC Lab @ Great Bay University team
hook: Live portrait animation, pure magic
pitch: PersonaLive lets you generate infinite-length portrait videos on the fly using a real-time diffusion framework. Run offline inference with just one command and get up to 100 frames by default, all in Python.

about: :cherry_blossom: A command-line fuzzy finder
hook: Fuzzy finder that feels like magic
pitch: A single-binary fuzzy finder that scans millions of items in milliseconds. It ships with ready-to-use integrations for Bash, Zsh, Fish, Vim and Neovim, so you can add fuzzy search to any script or editor instantly.

about: Command-line JSON processor
hook: Like sed, but for JSON
pitch: A tiny C-based CLI lets you slice, filter and transform JSON right from your shell. Grab a single field from a massive file with one short filter, and use prebuilt standalone binaries with zero runtime dependencies. 🚀

about: Virtual whiteboard for sketching hand-drawn like diagrams
hook: Diagrams that look hand-drawn
pitch: A browser-based infinite canvas that draws diagrams in a hand-sketched style. It supports real-time collaboration with end-to-end encryption and works offline as a PWA, all written in TypeScript.

about: An open-source cross-platform alternative to AirDrop
hook: AirDrop for every device
pitch: LocalSend lets you share files and messages over your local network without any internet or third-party servers. It works on iPhone, Android, Windows, macOS and encrypts every transfer with HTTPS. Just open the app and start sending.

about: Render markdown on the CLI, with pizzazz! 💅🏻
hook: Markdown, but make it pretty
pitch: Glow lets you view markdown right in the CLI, complete with colors, headings, and code blocks. It even lets you wrap lines with the -w flag, so you can set any width you like.

about: 🙌 OpenHands: AI-Driven Development
hook: AI dev team, right on your desk
pitch: OpenHands gives you a self-hosted control center that runs coding agents like Claude Code or its own OpenHands agent. Switch between local, Docker or cloud backends instantly, so your AI dev team is always on.

about: Minimal AI coding agent (~1,000 lines of Python) inspired by Claude Code. Works with any LLM. Think NanoGPT for coding agents. Formerly NanoCoder.
hook: Tiny AI coding agent in a notebook
pitch: A minimal Python AI coding agent that fits in a single notebook. The whole engine is just 1.3k lines, fully runnable with 215 green tests, so you can read, breakpoint, and extend it yourself.

about: #1 PDF Application on GitHub that lets you edit PDFs on any device anywhere
hook: PDF editing, anywhere you go.
pitch: A free, open-source PDF platform you can run anywhere—desktop, browser, or self-hosted. It offers 50+ tools like edit, merge, OCR, and a one-line Docker start command.

about: Real-time monitoring dashboard for Proxmox VE, PBS, Docker, Kubernetes, TrueNAS and vSphere. Self-hosted, with smart alerts and AI patrols that catch silent failures.
hook: Never-sleeping dashboard for your stack
pitch: Pulse gives you real-time views of Proxmox, Docker, Kubernetes and TrueNAS, with smart alerts that spot silent failures. Run it in seconds with a single Docker command.

about: JavaScript API for Chrome and Firefox
hook: Browser control, scripted instantly
pitch: Control Chrome or Firefox from JavaScript for testing and automation. No manual setup—just launch and go, and if install scripts are blocked, run npx puppeteer browsers install to fetch the browsers. 🚀

about: Open-source, Herd-like local PHP development environment for Linux and macOS. Automatic .test domains, per-project PHP/Node isolation, one-command TLS. Podman-native, rootless.
hook: Local PHP dev, zero Docker.
pitch: lerd gives you a root-less Podman setup for PHP projects. One command creates a .test domain with HTTPS and lets you switch PHP versions per project, plus one-click MySQL and Redis services.

about: Incredibly fast JavaScript runtime, bundler, test runner, and package manager – all in one
hook: JavaScript runtime that shatters Node speed
pitch: bun is a single-binary toolkit that runs, bundles, tests and installs JavaScript and TypeScript projects. It’s written in Rust, uses JavaScriptCore and supports TS + JSX out of the box, so you can replace Node with a tiny, speedy executable.

about: ODS V3 Pre-Release: Public testing and refinement ahead of the official V3 launch. Turn your PC, Mac, or Linux box into a private AI server.
hook: Private AI on your laptop.
pitch: ODS lets you spin up a local AI stack with a single command that auto-detects your GPU, selects the right model and launches the services. It’s Python-based, open-source and gives you instant chat while the full model downloads in the background.

about: Rich is a Python library for rich text and beautiful formatting in the terminal.
hook: Terminal library that makes code sparkle
pitch: rich lets you add color, emojis, tables and progress bars to any Python CLI. It even word-wraps output and highlights syntax out of the box, so your logs look clean and readable. Perfect for debugging and polished scripts.

about: A Kubernetes TUI, reimagined in Rust - built on kube-rs and ratatui, async-first from the ground up.
hook: Kubernetes cat watching your cluster
pitch: sofka is a Rust terminal UI that lets you browse custom resources, run bulk actions and open a deterministic incident view with a single key. It talks to Flux and Argo CD via API patches, no extra binaries needed. 🐱

about: A modern file manager that helps users organize their files and folders.
hook: A fresh take on Windows file browsing
pitch: Files is a modern Windows file manager that lets you tag files and use multitasking panes for quick navigation. Its fluent design blends right into Windows, boosting productivity.

about: Get tasks and ideas out of your head. A free GTD to-do app for desktop and mobile. Works offline, no account needed
hook: Someone built a to-do app offline.
pitch: A free, cross-platform GTD to-do app that lives completely offline. Capture ideas instantly with a desktop shortcut, phone widget, or share sheet, then organize, focus, and review without any account. Your data stays on your device.

about: Run your GitHub Actions locally 🚀
hook: Test GitHub Actions instantly
pitch: act lets you run your .github/workflows on your own machine, giving you fast feedback without pushing code. It uses Docker to spin up the same containers GitHub runs, so you can replace a Makefile with actions.

about: A persistent, Git-versioned map of your whole codebase and database schema that coding agents read before they touch anything. Local-first MCP server + CLI in Go: a governed repository index of code knowledge that gives Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and opencode long-term context, memory, and code intelligence.
hook: Someone built an instant code map
pitch: Creates a persistent, Git-versioned map of your whole codebase that AI coding agents can read in one pass. It can index repos up to 500 k lines and updates automatically as code changes. 📚

about: 🕷️ An adaptive Web Scraping framework that handles everything from a single request to a full-scale crawl! Don't be shy, join here: https://discord.gg/EMgGbDceNQ and follow here for daily tips and tricks: https://x.com/Scrapling_dev
hook: A scraper that learns as sites change
pitch: Scrapling is an open-source Python framework that learns from website updates and automatically relocates your selectors. It also includes fetchers that bypass Cloudflare Turnstile and a spider that handles proxy rotation and adaptive crawl speed.

about: Cross-platform local MCP capabilities for ChatGPT with Chrome integration, Goal, Compact & Resume, and durable multi-agent workflows.
hook: ChatGPT runs locally on your desktop
pitch: A cross-platform workspace lets you run ChatGPT right on your machine. Install, approve a folder, connect the Core in ChatGPT and load the Chrome extension – no extra servers needed. It’s open source and written in TypeScript.

about: A cat(1) clone with wings.
hook: Cat with wings for your terminal
pitch: bat adds syntax highlighting and Git-aware diffs to the classic cat command, so code pops with colors and changes are shown inline. Use the –show-all flag to reveal hidden whitespace and characters, all written in Rust.

about: Animation engine for explanatory math videos
hook: Math videos that dance
pitch: Manim lets you script every frame of a math animation in Python, so you get precise, programmatic control. Install it with a single pip command (pip install manimgl) and start rendering scenes right away. Perfect for anyone who wants clear code over keyframes.

about: Ministack: Free, open-source local AWS emulator - 60+ services, Terraform compatible, real databases. Free forever. MIT   licensed.
hook: Free AWS emulator you can run locally
pitch: Run 60+ AWS services on one port with no sign-up. It's drop-in compatible with boto3, the AWS CLI and Terraform, and uses real databases. Perfect for fast local testing and CI pipelines.

about: Improve viewing Markdown in Neovim
hook: Markdown preview lives inside Neovim
pitch: A Neovim plugin that renders Markdown right in the editor. Headings show icons, colors and padding, and code blocks display language icons with a background. All configurable and written in Lua.

about: A simple, lightweight PowerShell script that allows you to remove pre-installed apps, disable telemetry, as well as perform various other changes to declutter and customize your Windows experience. Win11Debloat works for both Windows 10 and Windows 11.
hook: Someone built a Windows declutter script.
pitch: A lightweight PowerShell script that strips pre-installed apps, disables telemetry and AI features, and lets you export/import your settings. Quick, no installation needed, and you can revert changes easily.

about: Storybook is the industry standard workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation
hook: UI workshop you can explore instantly
pitch: Storybook lets you build, test, and document UI components in isolation with live preview and auto-generated docs. It supports React, Angular, Vue, Svelte and more, all powered by TypeScript and a rich addon ecosystem.

about: 💥 Blazing fast terminal file manager written in Rust, based on async I/O.
hook: Terminal file manager like magic
pitch: yazi is a Rust-written terminal file manager that runs all I/O asynchronously, so navigating folders feels instant. It even shows image previews right in your terminal and lets you extend the UI with Lua plugins.

about: [READ ONLY] Official Appwrite React Native SDK 💙 ⚛︎
hook: React Native SDK that talks to the cloud
pitch: A TypeScript SDK that lets your React Native app talk directly to Appwrite services. It even supports background push notifications on Android, keeping users in the loop when the app isn’t active.

about: The fastest path to AI-powered full stack observability, even for lean teams.
hook: Monitoring that sees everything instantly
pitch: Netdata gives you per-second metrics and visualizations with zero configuration. It adds ML-powered anomaly detection while using minimal resources, scaling from a single server to multi-cloud fleets. Perfect for developers who need real-time observability.

about: TypeDB: Built for systems, not records
hook: A database that truly thinks like code
pitch: TypeDB lets you model data with a strongly-typed schema, so you get safety and flexible polymorphic queries. Its TypeQL language reads like natural language and supports reusable functions as subqueries. Built in Rust and fully open source, it unifies relational, document and graph models.

about: 🐹 Keep your Mac clean, light, and running like new. Fast open-source CLI, plus a native Mac app.
hook: Mac cleaning, finally simple.
pitch: Mole bundles deep cleaning, smart uninstalls and live system monitoring into one CLI. Run ‘mo clean’ to wipe caches and leftovers, or ‘mo analyze’ for an interactive TUI view of disk hogs. All free and open-source.

about: A personal timeline for quick notes. Write short memos, find them later by search, tag, or date. Open source and self-hosted.
hook: A timeline for your thoughts
pitch: Memos lets you jot down thoughts in Markdown, add images, and later find them by search, tags, or scrolling any day. It’s self-hosted, zero telemetry, and built with Go, so your data stays yours.

about: The Moby Project - a collaborative project for the container ecosystem to assemble container-based systems
hook: A Lego-style container toolkit
pitch: Moby gives you a modular container toolkit in Go, so you can pick and swap components just like Lego bricks. It ships with secure defaults and enough pieces to run a full container system out of the box.

about: Secure MCP runtime for AI agents to operate local machines, servers, and containers with multi-device orchestration.
hook: Secure AI bridge for your machines
pitch: AgentDock lets AI agents manage your local computers, servers and Docker containers straight from a chat. You can write code, run commands and orchestrate tasks across devices without leaving the conversation.

about: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent –  Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More
hook: Memory that never forgets
pitch: A TypeScript plugin that automatically captures, compresses, and re-injects agent observations so context survives across sessions. It even shows token cost with progressive disclosure and lets you query history via a skill-based search. 🚀

about: TAKT Agent Koordination Topology - Define how AI agents coordinate, where humans intervene, and what gets recorded — in YAML
hook: AI agents finally follow your script
pitch: takt is a CLI that lets you orchestrate AI coding agents with YAML-defined planning, implementation, review and fix loops. Each step runs in an isolated worktree and leaves traceable logs, so you get repeatable, auditable workflows.

about: Warp is an agentic development environment, born out of the terminal.
hook: A terminal IDE that thinks for you
pitch: Warp is a Rust-based terminal IDE with a built-in coding agent that answers prompts and lets you click into live web terminal sessions. It lets you bring your own CLI agents like Claude Code or Gemini.

about: A Rust library for building interactive prompts
hook: Rust prompts that feel magical
pitch: A Rust library that adds rich, interactive prompts to your CLI. Use Text with built-in autocompletion, open your editor for notes, or pick options with Select and MultiSelect—all cross-platform.

about: ✨ Zero-config AI chat assistant. No API key needed — sign up and instantly chat with GPT-5, Claude 4, Gemini 2.5, DeepSeek & 100+ top models. Pay-as-you-go saves you more. Available on Web, iOS, macOS, Android, Linux, Windows.
hook: AI chat that runs everywhere
pitch: Zero-config AI assistant that runs everywhere. Deploy it to Vercel with one click and get privacy-first local storage, markdown support, plus Claude, Gemini and GPT-5 models—all in a sleek TypeScript app.

about: AI that sees your screen, listens to your conversations and tells you what to do
hook: Screen-watching AI that never misses
pitch: omi captures your screen and conversation, transcribes live, and serves up summaries and action items. On macOS you can launch it with `git clone … && ./run.sh --yolo`. It’s open-source Python-based AI that works on desktop, phone and wearables.

about: Comfortably monitor your network traffic 🕵️‍♂️
hook: Network monitor made simple
pitch: Sniffnet lets you pick any network adapter and apply filters to watch traffic in real time. Export captures as PCAP files and see remote hosts plotted on a map, all from a cross-platform Rust app.

about: Prowler is the world’s most widely used open-source cloud security platform that automates security and compliance across any cloud environment.
hook: Someone built a cloud security platform
pitch: Prowler automates security and compliance checks across any cloud provider. Use the CLI with ‘prowler <provider>’ or spin up Prowler Cloud for an instant web UI dashboard. It’s open-source Python, so you can run it anywhere you need. 🚀

about: A new bootable USB solution.
hook: USB boot tool, no reformat needed
pitch: Ventoy lets you turn any USB, SSD, NVMe or SD card into a multiboot drive by simply copying ISO files—no formatting required. It boots directly from ISO or EFI and supports both MBR and GPT, all at copy-speed. 🚀

about: Zero-dependency browser video editor that AI agents can drive — JSON timeline, MCP + REST, live-reloading UI
hook: Video editing your AI can drive
pitch: FableCut is a zero-dependency, browser-based video editor whose whole timeline lives in a single JSON file. Let an AI agent like Claude write the JSON and watch the cuts appear live.

about: Open source alternative to AWS. Elastic compute, block storage (non replicated), firewall and load balancer, managed Postgres, K8s, AI inference, and IAM services.
hook: Run your own cloud, no lock-in.
pitch: Ubicloud gives you elastic compute, block storage and a built-in firewall on any bare-metal machine, all via a web console. It’s an open-source cloud platform written in Ruby, so you keep control and avoid lock-in.
